Lessons.Title: Paper Flower Decorations (optional)
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will create and analyze patterns in a real-world context and to solve multi-step problems.
This lesson is optional because it does not address any new mathematical content standards. This lesson does provide you with an opportunity to apply precursor skills of mathematical modeling. In this lesson, you build on your prior understanding and experiences with creating and analyzing patterns to solve multi-step problems in a real-world context.

Source activity sequence: Warm-up: How Many Do You See: Paper Flowers (10 minutes); Activity 1: Paper Flower Construction (15 minutes); Activity 2: Quinceañera Decorations (20 minutes); Activity 3: Make Your Own Problems (15 minutes)
Exact mathematical focus: Count complete pattern cycles and relate materials used to total flowers or garlands.

Edulytics authored model: A repeating pattern of 2 large and 2 small flowers has a 4-flower cycle. A 12-flower garland repeats this cycle three times: 6 large and 6 small. Four such garlands contain 48 flowers.
First-party Cool-down: Three garlands each need 12 flowers. How many flowers are needed?
Original diagrams, live construction, classroom response, and publisher login-gated Cool-down are not digitally certified.
